name: Conditional tactic rules
oneLiner: Every unit decides with an ordered list of rules, "condition → action (target)": ally HP under a threshold, a flying or armoured foe, a back-row target, self HP or MP, foe count, first turn. The first rule that holds and whose action is usable with a valid target wins, else the unit's Otherwise action. The evaluator is pure, deterministic and explains itself (which rule fired, why, and why each rule above it did not); players edit the list in a compact modal editor with class presets and a live "Now:" line, and a plate beside the acting unit names the rule and the target. The game's own skills, costs, reach and damage stay the game's: it plugs them in through adapters.
fits: turn-based RPG battle (enemy AI, party autoplay, auto-battle toggle)
tactics / strategy RPG (enemy phase, auto-move for player units)
squad auto-battlers and clash simulations (pure evaluate() for forecasts)
monster-taming and party RPGs with AI companions
real-time-with-pause party games (decide on each unit's action timer)
notFor: twitch action AI that reacts every frame (decide once per turn or action)
pathfinding or move planning (the game moves the unit; rules choose what to do and to whom)
dialogue or story branching (use H-02 dialogue choices)
learning or scoring AI that must search ahead (rules are a priority list, not a planner)

needs: the places where a unit's action is chosen (enemy AI, autoplay, auto commands), called once per unit turn
the game's skills with an aim (enemy, ally, self, all foes, all allies, none) and a role, plus usability (costs, items, cooldowns) and reach
unit fields: name, HP, max HP, MP, tags (flying, armoured, back row ...), class
a fixed update step that keeps running while the editor is open, a key and pointer route into the editor, and the unit sprite boxes and HUD rects on screen
provides: GameDNA_TacticRules.evaluate(rules, snapshot): a pure, explainable decision (action, target ids, rule fired, reason, trace)
decide(unit): the decision against the live game, with the game's own unit objects as targets
a modal rule editor (busy() while open) and a why plate with target ticks; rects() for other overlays
the rule book as plain JSON (exportBook / importBook) and debug events (decide with its snapshot, open, close, change)

assets: module/tactic-rules.js: the element as one dependency-free script (global GameDNA_TacticRules): pure evaluator, 13 conditions, 6 target picks, 5 role-based class presets, rule book, why plate with docking and target ticks, modal editor (keys, pointer, drag to reorder), smooth HD and crisp pixel drawing with built-in 5x7 / 3x5 bitmap fonts
no image, font or audio files (system sans stack, never loaded from the network)
